words.games.title: MLB Games
words.games.lede: Every MLB game, day by day: the betting line, the probable starters, where to watch, and the score as it happens.
words.rankings.title: MLB Standings
words.rankings.lede: The MLB standings, through games of {date}.
words.rankings.lede_goat: This site's own ranking of the 30 teams: ESPN's newest power ranking (half the score), strength of schedule, strength of record and head to head.
words.rankings.frozen: Final for the season: frozen at the end of the regular season.
words.rankings.lede_before: The season has not started yet.
words.rankings.note: Teams are placed by share of games won, then wins, then runs scored less runs allowed; the league's own tie-breakers are not worked through, so teams level on record can sit in a different order here. Records and runs are the league's, from ESPN, and count the regular season only. Choose a team to see its page.
words.rankings.note_conf: Seeds are ESPN's, as things stand: the three division winners, then the three best of the rest. The six teams above the line in each league make the playoffs.
words.rankings.note_goat: Every team is ranked on four things: its place in ESPN's newest power ranking (50%; the standings, until there is one), strength of schedule (20%: how good the teams it has played are, on average), strength of record (20%: a win counts for more the better the team beaten, a loss costs more the weaker the team lost to), and head to head (10%: a team is ranked above one it has the better of when the two are that close on the rest).
words.rankings.lede_nopoll: The season has not started yet.
words.rankings.note_other: Record and change are from the ranking itself.
words.teams.title: MLB Team Stats
words.teams.lede: How every MLB team hits, pitches and fields. From the box scores of the regular season.
words.teams.note: Hitting, pitching and fielding numbers count regular-season games with a box score. Rating is where this site's rating of results places the team in the league; SOS ranks every team by how strong its opponents have been. Choose a column heading to sort; hold or hover over a heading for what it means.
words.team.players_note: # is his rank by Impact among all MLB regulars: runs above average this season. Part-time players are greyed and not ranked. Choose a name for his card.
words.players.title: MLB Players
words.players.lede: Every regular in MLB, ranked against the rest by Impact: the runs he has been worth this season beyond an average regular in his job.
words.players.note: Impact is runs above average, from the box scores of the regular season. A hitter is measured against regulars at his position on what he does at the plate: 0.54 runs for a single, double or triple (a box score does not say which), 1.40 for a home run, 0.31 for a walk, and 0.26 lost for an out. A pitcher is measured against regular starters or relievers on the earned runs he gives up for the outs he gets. It cannot see fielding or baserunning, and it does not adjust for the ballpark or the opponent. On-base percentage and slugging are ESPN's.
words.players.none_yet: No box scores yet this season. Players appear here after the first games.
words.players.career_note: Each season's line is ESPN's, with a line for every team he has played for. It is read again after each of his team's games, so this season's line can be a game behind.
words.players.career_wait: His earlier seasons have not been read yet. They appear here within a day or two.
words.games.odds_short: These percentages are this site's own estimate of each team's chance of winning, not betting lines.
